proved_step: LEMMA B (unit-clause pinning = contraction, restricted form without auxiliary variables). Let the instance be c_i=(a_i,b_i), i in [m], and fix a unit constraint u with a_u = e_j, b_u = c (x_j = c). Let M be the binary matroid on {v_i : i != u} plus e, and let M/U be the contraction by U = v_u. Substituting x_j = c gives the system c'_i = (a'_i, b'_i) on n-1 variables, with a'_i = a_i restricted to coordinates != j and b'_i = b_i + a_{ij} c. Then the MUS clutter of the substituted system equals the port of M/U at e (as subsets of [m] minus u). Proof: phi(a,b) = (a restricted to coordinates != j, b + a_j c) is GF(2)-linear with kernel span{U}, since phi(e_j,c)=0 and phi(a,b)=0 forces a=t e_j, b=t c. Hence r_{M/U}(X) = r(X cup U) - r(U) = rank of phi(X), so M/U is the binary matroid of phi(v_i) plus phi(e) = e'. Lemma A applied to the substituted system finishes the proof. Hence the MUS clutter of the restriction x_j=c is the port of a minor (a contraction) of the original matroid, so port-preservation holds for unit-clause gadgets without auxiliary variables.

proved_step: LEMMA C (private-auxiliary gadgets, affine GF(2) case). Setting: original system with constraints c_i=(a_i,b_i), i in [m], H_i = {x in GF(2)^n : a_i.x=b_i}. For each i take a gadget E_i = a finite set of affine equations over (x, z_i), where z_i are auxiliaries PRIVATE to i (disjoint across i), such that proj_x sol(E_i) = H_i. Gadget system G = disjoint union of E_i, each equation owned by i. Claims: (i) G consistent iff original consistent; more generally for any owner set P, G|_P consistent iff original restricted to P consistent. (ii) For any S in G, let S_i = S cap E_i and P_i = proj_x sol(S_i). Then S is consistent iff no S_i is internally inconsistent and the intersection of the P_i is nonempty (private aux => lifts are independent). (iii) If a_i != 0 or b_i = 0 then P_i in {H_i, whole space, empty}, since an affine subspace containing a hyperplane is the hyperplane or everything. Internal inconsistency of S_i forces E_i inconsistent, i.e. a_i=0, b_i=1. (iv) Pushforward: if S is an MUS of G and no S_i is internally inconsistent, the owner set Q={i: P_i = H_i} is an original MUS. Proof: Q is inconsistent since the intersection of H_i over Q is empty. If Q' is a proper inconsistent subset of Q, pick j in Q minus Q'; deleting S_j makes the remaining intersection a subset of the intersection over Q', hence empty, so S is not minimal. Also owners with P_i = whole contribute no equations to an MUS, so S = union of S_j over j in Q. (v) Every original MUS M is realized: for each j in M choose a minimal T_j in E_j with proj = H_j; then union T_j is an MUS of G with owner set M. Scope: all gadget auxiliaries private to one constraint, affine (GF(2)-linear) gadgets only. Shared auxiliaries across constraints are NOT covered; G0001 stays open for that case. Lemma C does not claim anything about general Post-lattice languages.

proved_step: LEMMA R (repaired owner pushforward and realization for PRIVATE gadgets, arbitrary finite relations, scope limited to hypothesis R). Setting: constraints i in [m] with H_i a subset of X (x-domain); gadget E_i = finite set of relations over (x, z_i), z_i private to i, with pi(E_i) = H_i, where pi = projection to x. Consistent subsets T of E_i have pi(T) a subset of X. HYPOTHESIS R_i: every consistent T subset of E_i has pi(T) in {H_i, X}. Claim (a): if S is a minimal inconsistent subset of G = union of E_i and no S_i is internally inconsistent, then Q = {i : pi(S_i) = H_i} is an original MUS and S = union of S_j over j in Q. Claim (b): for every original MUS M there is a G-MUS with owner set M. Proof of (a): pi(S_i) contains H_i since S_i is a subset of E_i; by R_i, pi(S_i) is H_i or X. Private auxiliaries are disjoint, so a set is consistent iff the intersection of the owner projections is nonempty, hence the intersection over owners equals the intersection over Q of H_i. S inconsistent gives empty intersection over Q, so Q is nonempty and inconsistent. Owners outside Q have projection X and can be dropped without losing inconsistency, so minimality gives S = union over Q of S_j. For j in Q and e in S_j: S minus e is consistent, its owner-j projection is nonempty (else S minus e is internally inconsistent, contradicting minimality), so it is H_j or X by R_j. If it were H_j, the intersection would be the intersection over Q of H_i, which is empty, contradicting consistency. So it is X, giving intersection over Q minus j of H_i nonempty. Every proper subset of Q lies in some Q minus j, and consistency is monotone, so Q is minimal. Proof of (b): for j in M choose T_j minimal among subsets of E_j with pi(T_j) = H_j (H_j nonempty, so such T_j exists). Let S = union of T_j. Its owner projections are H_j, so S is inconsistent. For e in T_j, T_j minus e has nonempty projection set containing H_j and not equal to H_j by minimality, so it is X by R_j; then S minus e is consistent exactly when the intersection over M minus j of H_i is nonempty, which holds by minimality of M. So S is a G-MUS with owner set M. Remark (checked by hand): if H_i is a hyperplane of GF(2)^n (a single affine equation, the affine case), R_i holds automatically, since the only affine subspaces containing a hyperplane are the hyperplane and the whole space. This recovers S0003 (iii) for affine gadgets. Non-affine R fails on the H = {1} gadget example of cm-c792ee2f14a14a34. Scope: private auxiliaries; relations satisfying R for every constraint; does NOT claim R holds for the gadgets a Post-lattice pp-definition produces. Gap left open: which target relations admit R-gadgets (equivalently H_i is a coatom of the lattice of sub-projections of consistent subsets of E_i).

proved_step: LEMMA R-suff (sufficient condition for hypothesis R_i of S0009). Setting: finite X (x-domain) and Z; relations are subsets of X x Z, with pi the projection to X. Let E = {E_1,...,E_k}, k >= 1, with H = pi(intersection of all E_i) nonempty. CONDITION COND: for k >= 2 and every j, pi(intersection of E_i over i != j) = X. Claim: under COND, every nonempty T subset of E with intersection of T nonempty has pi(intersection of T) in {H, X}, i.e. hypothesis R holds for E. Proof: if T = E, the projection is H by definition. If T is a proper nonempty subset, pick j with E_j not in T. Then T is contained in E minus {E_j}, so intersection of T contains intersection of (E minus {E_j}) as sets of points. Projection is monotone, and the smaller intersection projects onto X by COND, so pi(intersection of T) = X. For k = 1 the only nonempty T is E. QED. Corollary: LEMMA R (S0009) applies to every private gadget family satisfying COND. Scope: COND is sufficient, not necessary (cond_fails_but_R_holds = 624 in the host record). It says nothing about which Post-lattice pp-gadgets satisfy COND, and it does not touch shared auxiliaries (G0001 stays open).

Hypotheses: (FUNC) for each i and each x in H_i, the Z_i-values of any solution of E_i over x are unique; write f_i(x). proved_step: Decoupling lemma for a shared existential bit. Setting: finite X; gadgets G_i subset of X x {0,1}; owner projection C_i = {x : exists z, (x,z) in G_i}; for T a set of gadget indices, shared(T) = {x : exists z, for all i in T, (x,z) in G_i} and owner(T) = intersection over i in T of C_i. Hypothesis (forced constants): for each i there is c_i in {0,1} with (x,z) in G_i implies z = c_i. Claim: if all c_i with i in T are equal to c, then shared(T) = owner(T); otherwise shared(T) is empty. Proof: if all c_i = c on T, then (x,z) in G_i forces z = c, so shared(T) = {x : (x,c) in G_i for all i in T}; and (x,c) in G_i iff x in C_i, because z is forced to c whenever x is in C_i. Hence shared(T) = owner(T). If c_i differ on T, no single z satisfies all gadgets in T, so shared(T) is empty. Scope: this is exact only for forced-constant gadgets, where the shared bit is already a constant and the formalization reduces to private gadgets with fixed values. It does NOT close G0001, which concerns shared bits not forced to a constant. proved_step: LEMMA P (private pp-gadgets preserve the MUS clutter). Setting: Boolean relations over a finite language Gamma; instance I = (X, (C_i)_{i in [m]}) with C_i = (R_i, u_i), u_i a tuple of variables from X. Assume each R_i has a pp-definition R_i(y) iff exists z phi_i(y, z), phi_i a conjunction of Gamma-constraints. Gadget G(I): fresh variables Z_1..Z_m, pairwise disjoint and disjoint from X; block i is phi_i(u_i, Z_i). Claim: for all S subset of [m], Sat(G(I)_S) iff Sat(I_S), where G(I)_S and I_S are the sub-instances on blocks/constraints in S. Consequently the minimal-unsatisfiable index sets coincide (MUS clutter preserved exactly). PROOF. (=>) Let a satisfy all blocks i in S. Restricting to X, for each i in S the tuple a|u_i satisfies exists z phi_i(., z), i.e. a|u_i in R_i, so a|X satisfies I_S. (<=) Let x satisfy I_S. For each i in S, x|u_i in R_i, so there is a witness w_i with phi_i(x|u_i, w_i). Set a = x on X and a = w_i on Z_i. Block i depends only on u_i and Z_i, and the Z_i are disjoint, so a satisfies every block in S. Hence Sat(G(I)_S). Both directions use only the pp-definition and disjointness; no restriction on Gamma, arity or m. Minimality of an index set is defined from the predicate Sat alone, so the MUS clutters agree. NON-TRIVIAL CONSEQUENCE / NECESSITY OF PRIVACY: with shared auxiliary z, the gadget system satisfies Sat(shared_S) implies Sat(I_S) (projection), so unsat(I_S) implies unsat(shared_S), but not conversely. Counterexample: R_A = {x: x=0} with gadget exists z (x=z and z=0); R_B = {y: y=1} with gadget exists z (y=z and z=1). I_{A,B} is satisfiable (x=0, y=1), while the shared gadget forces z=0 and z=1, so {A,B} becomes a spurious MUS. Scope: exact for private gadgets (the form used by pp-reductions of CSP instances, which substitute a fresh copy of a fixed gadget per constraint). statement: AFFINE CODIM-1 RECORD. Let n>=1, a in GF(2)^n nonzero, b in GF(2), H = {x : a.x = b}. Let E be a finite set of affine equations over (x, z), z = private auxiliaries (any number, any tuple), such that pi(sol E) = H where pi = projection to x and sol E is nonempty. Then for every subset T of E with sol T nonempty, pi(sol T) is H or the whole space GF(2)^n.
proof: (1) sol E is a subset of sol T, so pi(sol E) = H is a subset of pi(sol T). (2) Projection of a nonempty affine subspace of GF(2)^(n+|z|) under a linear map is an affine subspace of GF(2)^n; sol T is affine (solution set of a linear system) so pi(sol T) is affine. (3) H is an affine hyperplane (dimension n-1). Any affine subspace A with H subset of A has dim(A) in {n-1, n}; if dim n-1 then A = H, if dim n then A = whole space. Hence pi(T) in {H, X}. Q.E.D. Consequence: hypothesis R (of Lemma R, S0009) holds automatically for every affine private gadget whose target is an affine hyperplane; so Lemma R applies to all affine codim-1 targets without any check. statement: Shared-auxiliary GF(2) gadgets E_i(x,z) with H_i = {x : exists z E_i(x,z)}. If there is a function g such that E_i(x,z) iff (x in H_i and z = g(x)) for every owner i, then for every owner set P: {E_i : i in P} is consistent iff the intersection of H_i over i in P is nonempty.
proof: If (x,z) satisfies all E_i with i in P, then x lies in every H_i, so the intersection is nonempty. Conversely, if x lies in the intersection, then z = g(x) satisfies every E_i. Both directions are immediate from the definitions.

proved_step:
statement: Setting: GF(2), variables x in GF(2)^n and shared auxiliaries z in GF(2)^k. Owners i in [m] each contribute ONE equation a_i.x + b_i.z = c_i. Put vh_i = (a_i, b_i, c_i) in GF(2)^(n+k+1), let t = (0,...,0,1), and let E be the vector matroid on [m] plus e, with e mapped to t and i mapped to vh_i. For an owner set P, the subsystem {owners in P} is inconsistent iff t lies in span{vh_i : i in P}. The MUS clutter of the gadget system (minimal inconsistent owner sets) equals the port at e of this binary matroid.
proof: (1) Consistency. Let M be the (n+k)-column matrix with rows (a_i,b_i) for i in P, and c the vector of c_i. The system M y = c is solvable iff c lies in col(M). If c is not in col(M), there is lambda with lambda^T M = 0 and lambda.c = 1, so sum lambda_i vh_i = t. Conversely, if t = sum lambda_i vh_i, then lambda^T M = 0 and lambda.c = 1, so the system is unsolvable. Hence P is inconsistent iff t in span{vh_i : i in P}. (2) Port. Let X be a minimal subset of [m] with e in cl_E(X), i.e. r(X+e) = r(X), i.e. t in span(X). Then X+e contains a circuit C with e in C, and minimality forces X = C minus e. Conversely each circuit C through e gives C minus e as an inconsistent set, and the minimal ones are exactly the circuits through e minus e. So the MUS clutter is the port at e of E. (3) Each owner has exactly one equation, so a minimal inconsistent set of equations is a minimal inconsistent owner set, and the two clutters coincide. Loops (vh_i = 0) and parallel copies of t are handled by the same argument, since they give circuits of size 1 and 2 containing or avoiding e as appropriate.
scope: Exactly: GF(2) linear gadgets, one equation per owner, auxiliaries SHARED across owners. Covered by linear-matroid theory (classical; the step is a precise verified special case, not new mathematics). NOT covered: owners with two or more equations over shared z. There the owner clutter can be the port of U_{2,4} (not binary), see cm-f0a46fb95d764a4d and cm-7d3458c5d4a8460f, so the binary-port form fails for those owners. Consistent with cm-2918160065c34082, which tests the matroid-port form only for owners with 1-2 rows and m=3.

proved_step: S-COMMON-FUNCTION-OWNER-CLUTTER (CLAIMED, bookkeeping, closes nothing). Statement: let C_1..C_m be constraints on x in {0,1}^n, f: {0,1}^n -> {0,1}^k any fixed function, and G_i(x,z) := C_i(x) AND (z = f(x)) with one shared auxiliary block z. For every owner set S, {G_i : i in S} is satisfiable iff {C_i : i in S} is satisfiable; hence the owner-MUS clutter equals the original MUS clutter. Derivation: every solution (x,z) of the S-subsystem has z = f(x), so (x,z) solves it iff x solves {C_i : i in S}, and x -> (x, f(x)) is a bijection between the two solution sets. Satisfiability of every subset, and therefore minimal unsatisfiability, is preserved. Evidence: special case of H_common, cm-d3a069abe94d490b (0 of 1500 mismatches). Scope: exact for the semantic gadget only. It does NOT discharge G0001: the open point is whether the graph {(x, f(x))} is pp-definable in the target Post-lattice language Gamma, which is not established.

S-SHARED-Z-COMMUTATION (CLAIMED, restatement of the Galois correspondence, closes nothing). For f: {0,1}^n -> {0,1}^k and finite Boolean Gamma: graph(f) is pp-definable from Gamma iff f(g(x_1..x_r)) = g(f(x_1)..f(x_r)) for all g in Pol(Gamma) of arity r and all x_i. Proof: invariance of graph(f) under g is exactly this commutation; pp-definable relations are Pol-invariant; and Inv(Pol Gamma) equals the pp-closure of Gamma (Geiger; BCKSV). Consequence: the shared gadget z = f(x) is usable in Gamma only for f commuting with Pol(Gamma); for affine Gamma these are the affine maps. Evidence: cm-0d1388d5eb224886 (n=2, k=1; counts 8,5,5,6, hand-verified). Open: whether a non-trivial shared f commuting with the target Pol(Gamma) yields a port-preserving gadget for owner-MUS clutters.

evidence: Proof: a set T containing e is a circuit iff it is minimal dependent. For T = {e} u r_S, dependence means e in span(r_S), since e != 0 rules out the empty combination. Removing e leaves r_S, which is independent iff no proper subset of S already spans the same rank. Removing r_j leaves {e} u r_{S\{j}}, which is independent iff e not in span(r_{S\{j}}). These are exactly the conditions defining S, so the match is exact. Scope: single-row owners only. This is a standard matroid fact and closes no obligation. G0001 (shared auxiliaries with multi-row owners) remains open: the multi-row counterexample cm-9c543476bd7541c7, verified by cm-0c33bf85caa544f4, shows the port property fails for 2-row owners sharing z. proved_step: LEMMA R-aff (affine gadgets, hyperplane scope). Setting: X = GF(2)^k; constraint i has gadget E_i, a finite system of affine equations over (x, z_i), with z_i private to constraint i; pi = projection to x; H_i = pi(sol(E_i)) is assumed to be an affine hyperplane of X. Claim: for every T subset of E_i with sol(T) nonempty, pi(sol(T)) is H_i or X, so hypothesis R_i holds. Proof: T subset of E_i implies sol(T) contains sol(E_i), so pi(sol(T)) contains H_i. pi(sol(T)) is an affine subspace, being a linear image of an affine space. A hyperplane is a maximal proper affine subspace, so any affine subspace containing H_i is H_i or X. Scope: affine gadgets with H_i a hyperplane only. Not covered: H_i of codimension >= 2 (the 12 point-H violations in cm-7a7d151bb1f24830), and non-affine gadgets (G0001 open, 853 violations).

proved_step: LEMMA D (one-sided shared-auxiliary port, any finite relations over GF(2), no affineness used). Setting: constraints i with H_i a subset of X = GF(2)^n; gadget E_i a finite set of relations over (x, z) with z one SHARED auxiliary block; pi_x(sol(E_i)) = H_i. For S a set of constraints let G_S = union over i in S of E_i. Claim: if the original subsystem S is inconsistent (intersection over i in S of H_i is empty), then G_S is inconsistent. Proof: suppose (x,z) satisfies G_S. Then (x,z) satisfies each E_i with i in S, so x lies in pi_x(sol(E_i)) = H_i for every i in S, hence x lies in the intersection, which is empty. Contradiction. So every original-inconsistent subset stays inconsistent in the gadget system, and every original MUS contains a gadget-inconsistent set. Scope: this is the soundness direction only. The converse (gadget-inconsistent implies original-inconsistent) is exactly what fails for shared z: cm-2d1bfecd874342f9 gives the two-constraint counterexample with H_0 = H_1 = GF(2)^3 and gadgets {z=0} and {z=1}, and cm-f417cc87c52645a9 gives 918/3750 mismatches with free constants.

refuted_approach: Candidate (a) for the converse of G0001: 'each gadget's z-fibre over H_i is a single affine function f_i of x (graph)'. REFUTED by hand, using the counterexample cm-2d1bfecd874342f9. Take H_0 = H_1 = GF(2)^3, E_0 = {z = 0}, E_1 = {z = 1}. Each E_i is the graph of a constant function (f_0 = 0, f_1 = 1), so both satisfy (a), and each projects onto H_i. Yet E_0 union E_1 is inconsistent while the original intersection H_0 cap H_1 = GF(2)^3 is nonempty. So a graph condition alone cannot give the converse. Any repair must constrain how the fibre functions f_i relate to one another on the intersection, e.g. require f_i = f_j on cap_{i in S} H_i. That condition is compatibility itself, which the earlier check S-G0001-common-graph showed to be tautological, so it does not close G0001.

lemma: Lemma T (GF(2), restricted class, bookkeeping; closes no obligation). Occurrences are single equations a.x=b or bundles of equations sharing one linear part a. A bundle with all right-hand sides equal to b has the solution set of a.x=b and is replaced by w=(a,b); a bundle with differing right-hand sides has empty solution set and is replaced by w=e=(0,...,0,1). Claim: the occurrence-level MUS clutter of the system equals the port at e of the binary matroid on {w_i} plus e. Proof: by Lemma S (GF(2) Fredholm), a family of occurrences is inconsistent iff some T has sum of a-parts 0 and sum of b-parts 1, iff e lies in the span of the chosen w_i. Consistency depends only on the w_i, so minimal inconsistent occurrence sets are the minimal sets S with e in span(w_S), which are the circuits through e minus e. Scope: GF(2), any n, each occurrence a singleton or same-linear-part bundle; mixed linear parts NOT covered. Evidence: cm-1a2cb3072f61489b (singletons n=3 m=3 exhaustive 4096 systems, 0 fails; random n=4 m=2..5, 3200 systems, 0 fails; same-linear-part bundles n=3 m<=4, 3000 samples, 0 fails). This is a replication by a different method, not a proof of the general statement.

proved_step:
statement: Let V_i = span(v_i) in GF(2)^(N+1) for occurrences i in a finite index set I (each bundle is a single augmented equation, coefficients in (x,z), right-hand side last), t = (0,...,0,1). For S subset of I, the system {equations of i : i in S} is inconsistent iff t lies in span{v_i : i in S}. The minimal inconsistent occurrence sets are exactly the sets C minus {t}, where C ranges over the circuits of the binary vector matroid on {v_i : i in I} plus {t} that contain t.
derivation: (1) Fredholm alternative for GF(2) affine systems: a system with augmented rows v_i (right-hand side last) is unsolvable iff some GF(2)-combination of its rows is 0 = 1, i.e. iff t in span{v_i : i in S}. (2) If S is minimal with t in span(S), then S is independent (otherwise a proper subset already spans) and S union {t} is dependent with a unique expression of t; hence S union {t} is a circuit containing t. (3) Conversely, a circuit C containing t gives S = C minus {t} with t in span(S), and minimality follows because a proper subset of S spanning t would yield a smaller dependent set containing t, contradicting circuit minimality. Zero vectors v_i = 0 (trivially satisfiable equations) are in no circuit and are excluded. Case v_i = t gives the singleton circuit {i, t}, i.e. S = {i}, consistent with the statement.
scope: Rank-1 bundles only (each occurrence contributes one linear equation). Finite, exact. Does NOT cover bundles of rank >= 2, and does NOT cover shared auxiliaries in the rank >= 2 setting (counterexample cm-c960a57e095a4e0e shows the interface identity fails there).
closes: none (sharpens Q-e8ef90900d; does NOT close G0001)

proved_step: LEMMA (fiber identity, hand-proved; CLAIMED, not reviewed): owners i in [m] with S_i subset of X x Z, A_i^z = {x : (x,z) in S_i}. For nonempty T, the intersection over i in T of S_i is empty iff for every z in Z the intersection over i in T of A_i^z is empty. Proof: (x,z) lies in the joint intersection iff x lies in every fiber intersection at z. Consequence: the joint MUS clutter is the minimal elements of the intersection over z of the fiber up-sets U_z, and it is not the union or intersection of the per-fiber clutters. Counterexample: X={0,1}, Z={0,1}, S_0 = X x {0}, S_1 = X x {1}. Then {0,1} is minimal in U_0 cap U_1 while min(U_0) = {{1}}, min(U_1) = {{0}}. This closes no obligation: it is a structural diagnosis, not a repair of G0001.
